transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-08
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Ng (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Helios ML), Marcus Lee (Helios Platform), Lauren Chen (CTO)

Auto-generated Summary:
Helios is scoping a 6-week POC to validate latency and throughput SLOs for patient-facing summarization and search features. Primary focus is on defining TTFT (time-to-first-token) and TPOT (time-per-output-token) targets at p95/p99 under representative concurrency, plus measurement plan for cold vs warm cache and model routing fallbacks. Action items: Redwood to share benchmark harness and test matrix; Helios to share workload samples and access for staging runs.

Topics:
- Definitions: TTFT vs TPOT
- Target SLOs (p95/p99) for interactive and batch workloads
- Measurement plan: cold vs warm, concurrency, priming, KV cache effects
- Success criteria for pilot and pass/fail thresholds
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining on time. quick intros - i'm samir from redwood, ae on your account, and jules is our se who will run the bench stuff.
[00:08] Jules: hi all, hi priya, marcus, lauren, good to meet you. we'll focus today on the slos and how you want us to measure them.
[00:15] Priya: hi, glad to be here. our main ask is low latency for the summarization UI — users expect near instant responses, but we also have nightly batch reranking where throughput matters.
[00:25] Lauren: multiple stakeholders: product cares about first-response speed, platform cares about cost/throughput, security/commpliance is a separate stream.
[00:35] Marcus: we host most customer data in GCP, we'll likely run Redwood private in a VPC or dedicated; but for the POC we can use hosted. security paperwork is pending but doable.
[00:46] Samir: perfect. to ground the convo, can you give us the expected QPS and typical prompt sizes?
[00:52] Priya: interactive: peak ~30 concurrent users hitting summarization, average prompt tokens ~120, output ~80 tokens. background batch: about 5k docs over a 2 hour window; each doc prompt ~400 tokens and output ~350.
[01:10] Jules: good, that helps. on latency metrics we typically separate TTFT and TPOT — quick defs: TTFT is time-to-first-token, includes scheduling, model load and initial kernel execution; TPOT is time-per-output-token once streaming begins, it's the incremental per-token latency. some customers call TPOT tpt or time-per-token.
[01:31] Priya: ok that matches our terminology. what targets do you usually see for p95/p99?
[01:37] Jules: depends on model and hardware. for medium-sized open models on GPU, a typical interactive target we recommend is TTFT p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 350ms; TPOT p95 <= 10ms, p99 <= 20ms for long-running decoding on optimal hardware. for smaller quantized variants on A100-like hardware those numbers can be lower.
[02:01] Marcus: those TTFT numbers seem reasonable. our UX folks want p95 under 150ms ideally for first token. is that realistic for 120-token prompts?
[02:10] Jules: for 120-token prompts, with prefix/KV cache warmed and on p4/a10 style hardware, p95 around 120-150ms is achievable for some LLaMA-family variants. But cold-start and model swapping can push you higher.
[02:24] Samir: we should define measurement buckets: cold TTFT (no KV cache, instance spin-up), warm TTFT (shared pool, KV cache primed), and steady-state TPOT under target concurrency. also need p95/p99 for both interactive and batch run-throughput.
[02:39] Lauren: define cold vs warm clearly - for us cold means long tail when a model variant hasn't had any requests in last 30 minutes, warm means seen at least one request in last 5 minutes.
[02:50] Jules: we'll adopt those windows. measurement plan proposal:
- Step 1: synthetic replay using your prompt set at 1x, 5x, and 10x expected traffic; measure TTFT/TPOT per request with timestamps.
- Step 2: run cold-start tests where we scale pool to zero and send single request, measure time to first token across 100 samples.
- Step 3: warm-run with KV cache primed: send warm primers then run concurrency sweeps (1,5,10,20 concurrent) and capture p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and TPOT.
- Step 4: batch throughput test: sustained TPUT calculation for bulk jobs (docs/hour) with model quantization variants.

[03:30] Priya: can you explain how you measure TPOT precisely? some vendors report average token time which hides the tail.
[03:37] Jules: yes, we capture per-token timestamps at generation time. TPOT p95 is the 95th percentile of inter-token intervals after first token; we also report p50 and p99. we include network overhead and client-side streaming latency if you want end-to-end numbers, or server-only if you prefer instrumentation inside the runtime.
[03:55] Marcus: prefer server-only for isolation, but also want end-to-end numbers to understand UX impact.
[04:01] Samir: we'll provide both. important to note: TPOT can vary based on sequence length requested (longer contexts increase memory pressure and can change kernel selection), so our test matrix will sweep prompt and output lengths.
[04:14] Lauren: what's the recommended pass/fail criteria for the POC? product wants p95 TTFT <= 150ms and p95 TPOT <= 12ms for interactive; platform wants cost per 1k tokens under $X — we'll refine cost target later.
[04:29] Jules: candidly, for a first pass we recommend pragmatic thresholds:
- Interactive: TTFT p95 <= 200ms (stretch 150ms), TTFT p99 <= 350ms; TPOT p95 <= 15ms, TPOT p99 <= 30ms.
- Batch: end-to-end throughput measured as docs/hour and average token cost; p95 latency per doc < 4s for typical 350-token outputs.

[04:55] Priya: fine, product will push for 150ms, but engineering accepts 200ms as baseline. we'll aim for stretch goals.
[05:03] Samir: good, we'll target baseline and list stretch objectives in the report. now on measurement artifacts: Jules, will you walk through what we'll deliver?
[05:10] Jules: yes - deliverables: benchmark harness (k6 + custom generator) with your prompt sets, a README for running tests, dashboards for p50/p95/p99 for TTFT/TPOT, and raw CSVs with per-request and per-token timestamps. We'll also produce a test matrix doc that enumerates cold vs warm, concurrency levels, model variants, and quantization.
[05:32] Marcus: about KV cache: do you prime KV cache per user/session? how do you simulate per-user cache levels?
[05:38] Jules: we support prefix/KV caching strategies. for the POC we can simulate user sessions where primers include the last N tokens to populate KV cache; we'll run separate sweeps for per-session cached vs shared cache. note that per-session caches reduce TTFT significantly for follow-up queries.
[05:56] Priya: another measurement we care about is tail latency when routing fallback happens — e.g., if a preferred model is unavailable we fallback to a smaller quantized variant. how will you capture that?
[06:06] Jules: we'll include fault-injection cases: simulate model pool saturation and observe fallback latency distribution. we'll mark those requests in the data and report them separately. often fallbacks increase TTFT substantially but keep throughput available.
[06:18] Lauren: good — we need a runbook describing expected behavior and user-visible degradations.
[06:23] Samir: we'll include that in the final report. next: timeline — Helios wants a 6-week POC with a 2-week baseline, 2-week tuning, 2-week validation and handoff. does that align?
[06:34] Marcus: yes that's workable. security/legal gating may affect start date; we should assume a 1-2 week lead on paperwork.
[06:41] Samir: timeline we'll propose: Week 0: alignment and access; Week 1-2: baseline runs and initial report; Week 3-4: tuning model variants, quantization, batching policies; Week 5-6: validation, robustness tests (cold starts, fallbacks), and final handoff.
[06:59] Priya: can we include cost experiments — e.g., batching and quantization effects on cost/latency tradeoffs?
[07:05] Jules: absolutely. we'll add a cost-vs-latency matrix: for each config we'll report tokens/sec and $/1k tokens, and show Pareto frontier for your workload.
[07:16] Samir: any legal or security blockers for hosted infra? Marcus?
[07:19] Marcus: general SOC2/ISO are fine, we will require data residency and KMS integration for production. for POC we can use hosted with opt-in logging and retention.
[07:31] Samir: noted. we'll share our security package alongside the benchmark harness.
[07:36] Priya: small question on measurement: do you include cold-model compile/first inference JIT times in TTFT?
[07:42] Jules: yes we include compile and kernel selection times in cold TTFT. for warm TTFT, compile cost is amortized away. we'll label the metrics accordingly: server-only cold-ttft, warm-ttft, and end-to-end including network e2e-ttft.
[07:57] Lauren: ok. also want to ensure reproducibility — can we get the harness and exact seed/config so we can re-run on our side?
[08:04] Jules: we'll provide config files, container images for the client driver, and an instrumentation README. reproducibility is a priority.
[08:12] Samir: quick note about p99: p99 often dominated by outliers — we typically look for patterns (GC, noisy neighbor, cold start). we'll include traces for requests in the p99 bucket so you can diagnose.
[08:25] Priya: super helpful. one more thing — we have a live demo environment simulating 1% of production traffic; can we run a verification there before moving to dedicated?
[08:33] Samir: yes, we can. if you provide credentials we'll run a light smoke test and baseline.
[08:38] Marcus: i'll work with security to create a service account with limited scope.
[08:42] Samir: great. any other questions?
[08:45] Priya: how do you handle tokenization mismatches across model variants? we want to ensure output lengths are comparable when measuring TPOT.
[08:52] Jules: we'll normalize by measuring tokens with the model's tokenizer and report both byte-lengths and token counts per model. we'll include an alignment step in the harness so you can compare apples-to-apples.
[09:02] Lauren: final quick ask: include a suggested SLO doc we can present to product with recommended baselines and stretch goals.
[09:08] Samir: yes, part of the deliverables.
[09:12] Wrap / Recap:
Samir: recap of next steps: Samir will send harness + readme; Jules will send test matrix and measurement plan; Priya will share prompt sets; Marcus will provision access; we target baseline runs week of 2026-04-15.
[09:30] Lauren: sounds good. thanks all.
[09:33] Meeting ends.

Notes on measurement plan (post-call summary):
- Metrics to capture: TTFT (cold/warm/e2e), TPOT (per-token p50/p95/p99), throughput (tokens/sec), cost per 1k tokens, fallback frequency and cost impact, cold-start time distribution, and per-request traces for p99 analysis.
- Test matrix dimensions: model variant (full/quantized), warm vs cold, concurrency (1,5,10,20), prompt length (short/medium/long), output length, priming/session cache settings, routing/fallback scenarios, and network e2e vs server-only instrumented runs.
- Data artifacts: per-token timestamp CSVs, aggregated percentiles, dashboards (Grafana/Looker), raw logs, and a final report with recommendations and code/config to reproduce.

End of transcript.
